name: WebAssembly
description: WebAssembly (Wasm) is a low-level binary instruction format that runs at near-native speed in browsers and beyond. It enables compiling C/C++, Rust, Go, and other languages to run on the web and in edge runtimes.

items.title: MDN WebAssembly Guide
items.description: The premier WebAssembly guide from Mozilla — covers concepts, compilation, JavaScript API, and text format.

items.title: Wasm By Example
items.description: A hands-on guide with annotated code snippets in Rust, AssemblyScript, and Go showing practical Wasm patterns.

items.title: WebAssembly.org Docs
items.description: The official home of the WebAssembly standard with developer guides and architecture details.

items.title: W3C WebAssembly Core Specification
items.description: The official W3C specification for the WebAssembly virtual machine.

items.title: WebAssembly for Beginners (Linux Foundation)
items.description: A free course on WebAssembly design, architecture, security, and real-world use cases.

items.title: WebAssembly Course (Frontend Masters)
items.description: An intermediate course covering Wasm compilation, memory, and browser integration.

items.title: WebAssembly Talks (YouTube)
items.description: Conference talks from Wasm community covering production use cases and ecosystem updates.

items.title: WasmFiddle++
items.description: Online sandbox for writing C/C++, compiling to Wasm, and testing in the browser.

items.title: MDN Wasm Reference
items.description: Complete reference for WebAssembly instructions, types, and module definitions.

items.title: Wasm Weekly
items.description: A curated weekly newsletter covering Wasm articles, projects, and ecosystem updates.

items.title: Reddit r/WebAssembly
items.description: Community for Wasm discussions, project showcases, and technical Q&A.
